mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past 3 months signals an easing monetary policy that lowers discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods with 3-month FEDFUNDS decline, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment rate rises above 4.7% in a single month, it signals labor market deterioration that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of months with UNRATE > 4.7%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous FEDFUNDS increase and UNRATE decline signals monetary tightening amid strong labor market, compressing corporate margins and raising borrowing costs, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
regime_hint: tightening cycle with strong labor market
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods with FEDFUNDS↑ and UNRATE↓, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion (UNRATE < 4.0%), a decline in residential construction permits (HOUST) signals housing sector slowdown that reduces consumer wealth and corporate revenue, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of late-cycle periods with HOUST decline, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: When residential construction permits (HOUST) fall below 1250 thousand units, it indicates housing sector contraction that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of months with HOUST < 1250, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: In high-employment regime (UNRATE < 4.0%), a decline in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals labor market slowdown that reduces consumer spending and corporate hiring, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of high-employment periods with PAYEMS decline, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) over 3 months indicates robust manufacturing activity that supports corporate earnings growth, producing positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods with 3-month INDPRO increase, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: When year-over-year CPI (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 2.5%, it signals accelerating inflation that triggers Fed tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of months with CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year windows.
